TRAFFIC ADVISORY
18/09/25

This is to inform the FCT motoring public of another rounds of flag-off and commissioning of projects in the FCT from 18 September to 16th October 2025 by the Honourable Minister of FCT, his Excellency Chief (Barr) Ezenwo Nyesom Wike CON.

As such there will be slight traffic disruption in some locations around the FCT.

On 18th September 2025, the Gidado Idris/Tunde Idiagbon junction, Wuye District, will be the venue of the flag-off of the construction of arterial Road N1 from Wuye District to Ring Road ii.

Traffic along these routes will be under control by traffic and security personnel for seamless movement of dignitaries, and deployment will be at 8am.

— Head Traffic, DRTS

data.raw_text:
It’s been a minute.

The Philippines is currently experiencing one of its biggest corruption scandals in recent memory. 

Ghost projects are at the center of the Philippines' massive flood control corruption scandal. From ‘22 to ‘25, flood control projects were allocated an enormous budget exceeding P1.09 trillion, roughly, $17-18 billion. 

How the scheme works: government engineers approve massive budgets for flood control projects, contractors submit winning bids, funds are released, but the actual infrastructure is never built or only partially completed with substandard materials. The money simply disappears into private pockets while Filipino communities remain vulnerable to flooding.

The scandal has reached the highest levels of government. 

As this exploded in public, Philippine lawmakers simultaneously began filing blockchain transparency bills:

Senate:
• Sept 2, 2025: Senator Paolo "Bam" Aquino files Senate Bill 1330, the "Blockchain the Budget Bill"

House:
• Sept 8, 2025: Rep. Javier Miguel "Javi" Benitez files House Bill 4380, the "Blockchain the Budget Act”

• Sept 9, 2025: Rep. Brian Poe Llamanzares files House Bill 4489 “National Budget Blockchain System”

• Sept 16, 2025: Rep. Charisse Hernandez files House Bill 4611 “An Act Mandating the Use of Blockchain Technology in the Formulation, Implementation, and Monitoring of the Government Budget to Promote Open Governance and Citizen Engagement”

Why Ghost Projects Make Blockchain Inevitable

The national scandal creates the perfect conditions for adoption.

Transparency: ghost projects thrive in opacity - projects are approved, funded, and "completed" without public visibility into any work being done

Audit: the current system allows money to flow directly from budget allocation into contractor payments without immutable records of actual deliverables

Political necessity: the scale of corruption will encourage politicians to support transparency measures they might have previously resisted

What might have taken a decade of advocacy is being fast-tracked in mere months by the scale of this theft. 

The country is in position to leverage the current corruption crisis as an opportunity to build towards greater fiscal accountability. And maybe becoming one of the world's first blockchain-transparent government. 

It shows that blockchain doesn't get adopted bc “gud tek” or “VC backed”, we get adoption when the crisis in infrastructure becomes so blatant (and expensive) that politicians and other stakeholders have no choice but to embrace transparency. 

Whether you’re in Brazil, Nigeria, India, Indonesia, or anywhere else in the world dealing with any kind of infrastructure problem, the same catalyst can exist in your backyard. Beyond green candles, let’s not forget what this emerging tech enables, and what it might do for our local communities.

I’m standing by what I said in Abu Dhabi (and quoting @jackbutcher): 

“When we eliminate ego, great things happen.” 

Blockchain does not make us better than anyone; if anything it’s a responsibility to politely, calmly, gently mention what blockchain can do for all of us. Let’s leave ego out the door. And those in our family, workplaces, strangers, who don’t yet understand blockchain, it’s like a responsibility for us to simplify it to them. 

Eventually, people will understand. Blockchain is for everyone
